clips.title:
Ask for a *picture* before
you send your pump truck

youtube.title: Septic customer says the tank needs pumping? Ask for a picture first

captions.facebook:
Picture this: water is backing up into the house, and the homeowner is sure the septic tank needs to be pumped right now. {kim} of {nawt}, who runs a septic pumping business with her husband in Colorado, asks one question first: have you looked inside your septic tank? If it's at the correct level, she says you can pump it all day long and it won't fix anything, because the blockage is in the main line. These days she has people send a picture of what they're looking at, and she tells them whether they have a problem or not.

#septic

clips.title:
A septic clog fixed
from *Disney World*

youtube.title: He Talked a Septic Customer Through a Clog From Disney World

captions.facebook:
{kim} of {nawt} runs a septic pumping business with her husband Jeff, and his dad would never take a vacation. Jeff was a lot like him, so getting him to Disney World was a big deal. She has a picture of him sitting on a bench in the park, on the phone, talking a customer through a blockage in his line. The customer did exactly what Jeff said and called back a few minutes later: you're at Disney and you're telling me how to unplug my septic system. Kim says that kind of customer service has been lost in recent years.

#septic

clips.title:
The septic install mistake
Colorado *kept finding*

youtube.title: The Septic Install Mistake Colorado Inspectors Kept Finding
Septic Installers and Pumpers Know More Than They Think

captions.facebook:
{kim} of {nawt} has seen it for years in her trainings. The guys used to say, I'm just an installer, I'm just a pumper. And now she tells them, no, you're not just that. You see what works and what doesn't, so you know more about the system than some designers and some regulators. If you take that information back to them, she says, you help them help themselves. That kind of confidence is something a lot of people in this industry deserve to hear.

#septic

clips.title:
Be the septic company
they *call first*

youtube.title: Be the Septic Company Homeowners Call First

captions.facebook:
Think about who is actually in charge of a septic system. It's the homeowner, and they're also the least educated person about it. {kim} of {nawt} says that's why it matters so much for the pros to become the resource those homeowners call first. Instead of calling grandpa, who has lived on a septic system and never pumped it, they call somebody who knows those systems. She says it's good for business, good for the homeowner and good for the system.

#septic

youtube.title: Septic Customers Hang Up Fast. Answer the Phone.

captions.facebook:
When wastewater starts backing up into the house, people go straight into panic mode. The first thing they do is pick up the phone and dial a septic company. If nobody answers, they hang up and call the next one down the line. {kim} of {nawt} has run a septic pumping business for years, and her advice is simple: if you want people to call you, you better answer the phone.

#septic
